newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end softer on select blue-chip selling.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end softer on select blue-chip selling.

text.p: Malaysian stocks ended lower on Thursday as foreign and local funds selectively sold down blue chips, dealers and analysts said.
Small cap stocks continued to slide down.

"Genting and Resorts World have both seen profit taking, which has brought the (Composite) Index down, while Sime Darby was up, preventing it from dropping further," said Razani Radzi, research manager at PB Securities.
Dealers said foreign fund managers had been buying select blue chips for around the last two weeks. The benchmark Composite Index was down 3.07 points to 1,231.10.
Genting was down 40 to 18.10, Resorts World was down 20 to 13.10, while Sime Darby was up five to 9.45. United Engineers was up 30 to 23.30 on foreign portfolio buying.

"U.S. funds have been in the market today, coming through from Hong Kong. This is part of their second tranche of buying," said a dealer at a local bank-backed securities house. "But the buying has not been aggressive," he added.

"Arab Malaysian Merchant bank had been chased up after its results, and is now being sold down, as had Commerce Asset," said the dealer. Arab Malaysian was down 1.10 ringgit to 20.80 ringgit, and Commerce Asset fell 50 cents to 18.80.
